title: Why Your Brain Sees Faces in Clouds
hook: Your brain constantly invents faces out of random shapes.

narration.text: Your brain constantly invents faces out of random shapes.
This is called pareidolia, where you perceive patterns in noise.
It is not a trick; your brain is wired to recognise faces instantly.
Even two dots and a line can trigger this recognition.
It helped our ancestors spot predators or friends in dim light.
Next time, look up at the clouds and see what you find.
Try it right now and tell me what you see in the comments, and like this if it surprised you; subscribe for more insights into your amazing mind, and send this to someone who always spots faces.

description: Ever wondered why you spot faces or familiar patterns in random clouds or objects? It is a fascinating trick of your brain called pareidolia. This video explains the science behind why your mind does this.
topic: Why your eyes sometimes trick you into seeing patterns or faces in random clouds. Look up and see if you can spot any.
